dod_intent_evidence: Real DoD motion exists — an Air Force 2023 SBIR Phase II ($1,249,955) for RAISR tied to ABMS, plus 2024 Phase I SBIR/STTR awards (ASTROEDGE, BASE-TWIN) — but the company sells engineering hours, not a product.
score_evidence: "We provide comprehensive software engineering services for multi-domain command and control, platform-level autonomy, and data management" → services business, stated on the homepage headline
"We provide comprehensive consulting services to implement AI-enabled hardware and software solutions." → LinkedIn about, and LinkedIn industry is Professional Services

Their pricing page sells labor, not software: "we are happy to provide a free 1-hour consultation... our Solution Prototype Starter Package for $800, where we: Match you with a senior engineer dedicated for a full day"

The "Products" page is actually headed "Products and Past Projects" and every entry is a past engagement description ("We have a history of deploying decentralized C2...", "We addressed critical challenges in Electronic Warfare (EW) modeling, simulation, and hardware test") → no owned product with a transition at stake
"The prototypes created have helped guide reliable software implementations into the DoD" → they hand prototypes to others to implement; nine people across six states, a distributed consulting bench
what_they_do: A nine-person distributed software-engineering consultancy that prototypes multi-domain C2, autonomy and sensor-processing solutions for Air Force and Space Force customers under SBIR and services contracts.
